- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing recent price momentum.
- Overshoots occur after large upward price movements in history; model reacts too aggressively, peaking too early and then falling.
- Mean reversion is overestimated — model assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly, ignoring persistent trends.
- Forecasts for the last 5–10 days of the 30-day window are often too high, especially when true outcomes show downward correction.
- Model exhibits bias toward lower values when history includes recent low prices, underreacting to rebounding trends.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to short-term volatility; model overreacts to minor price swings, leading to erratic predictions.
- When history shows a strong upward trend, model tends to overestimate the continuation, failing to account for potential reversal or consolidation.
